subject: Retention & KMS escrow: request for audit log streaming + BYOK exception
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@openhealth.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Ben —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. OpenHealth is moving quickly toward a pilot and we ran the compliance checklist with our security team overnight. Two items are blocking our internal approval: 

1) We need continuous audit log streaming (immutable) for all inference requests and policy events to our S3 bucket (us-east-1) for at least 7 years.
2) For regulatory reasons we must use our own KMS key (BYOK) for envelope encryption of persistent logs; we understand runtime model keys can remain managed, but logs must be encrypted with our key and we need key rotation visibility (audit on key usage).

Can Redwood support streaming audit logs directly to a customer-owned sink encrypted with a customer key, and provide signed evidence of key usage/rotation? If not, what compromise can get us to a pilot (we're asking for a time-limited exception if needed). I've attached our brief requirements.

Appreciate a quick triage — we are hoping to close procurement by month-end.

—Daniel
OpenHealth, Head of Security

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-11-18T10:03:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Looping in product & legal/security for triage. External ask from OpenHealth (attached requirements): long-term immutable audit stream to customer S3 + BYOK for log encryption and rotation visibility. They want to close procurement fast.

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: feasibility and product-level gaps (audit export, retention TTLs, compliance SLOs).
- Karthik: security constraints and proposed implementation options (customer-owned sink + envelope encryption, signing evidence).
- Lauren: contract/exception path — what can we commit to and what needs a formal exception/PoC term?

Goal: propose one pilot-friendly compromise we can promise in writing within 48 hours.

Thanks — will coordinate customer update once we have an internal approach.

-ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Thanks Ben — quick product read:

Summary of current platform capabilities that map to the ask:
- Audit log export: we have streaming export to customer S3 for operational logs (configurable retention on their side), but it is currently signed/host-managed (we push via our exporter service). We do not today encrypt the pushed objects with a customer KMS key at write time — objects are server-side encrypted using our infra keys.
- Retention semantics: we support TTLs and retention snapshots internally, but 7-year immutable retention backed by our platform requires an "archival" path and product-level retention SLA (not current standard offering).

Feasible pilot compromise (low product lift):
1) Enable streaming of audit events to customer S3 via our exporter, but write objects payload encrypted client-side by Redwood using a one-time envelope key we wrap with the customer's KMS (we can implement an S3 PutObject where the object body is already encrypted with envelope key provided by Redwood and then re-wrapped by customer KMS). This avoids storing unencrypted logs in our infra.
2) Provide signed, time-stamped usage records for each wrap/unwrap operation (an audit bundle with HMAC + timestamp + Redwood signature) to give the customer cryptographic evidence of key usage.
3) For the 7-year immutability ask: recommend using combined approach — customer-managed S3 object lock (governed via their bucket policies) + retention archive in Glacier or their chosen archive, since Redwood cannot guarantee 7-year on platform product logs without a new SLA/product.

Open questions for security/legal: can we ship the wrapping evidence (signature + timestamp) as contractual evidence? Also need to scope performance impact and cost for high-volume customers.

If we agree, engineering can scope a small PoC: ~3 sprint effort to wire up client-side encryption + signed usage records.

- Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Technical constraints and proposed secure compromise: 

Constraints:
- We do not run customer KMS keys in our control plane; we can call out to external KMS (customer or cloud) for wrapping/unwrapping but must avoid long-term custody of plaintext keys.
- Direct server-side encryption with a customer KMS across our exporter service introduces high latency at high throughput (each PutObject would require a WrapKey call).
- Immutable retention guarantees (regulatory-level) are outside current product SLAs — would need product/legal SLA and separate billing.

Proposed compromise (min-risk, pilot path):
A) Push encrypted payloads to customer S3 where Redwood performs client-side envelope encryption. Process:
  - Redwood generates a per-batch ephemeral data key (DEK).
  - DEK is wrapped by calling the customer's KMS via a cross-account role (customer must permit Redwood principal to call kms:Encrypt on their CMK).
  - Encrypted objects (ciphertext) are uploaded to customer S3; Redwood never stores plaintext objects post-upload.
  - Redwood records a signed wrap record (timestamp, key-id, DEK-wrapped-ciphertext-hash, request-id) and ships that record to customer in parallel.

B) Evidence and rotation visibility:
  - Customer KMS audit logs (CloudTrail) will show Redwood principal calling Encrypt; we can augment with our signed wrap records as corroborating evidence.
  - For rotation visibility, we will include key-id and wrap-timestamp in signed wrap records. If customer rotates the CMK, future wrap records will reference the new key-id.

Operational asks from customer:
- Add Redwood IAM principal to their KMS policy for Encrypt only on the CMK used to wrap data keys.
- Configure S3 bucket policies to accept PutObject from Redwood exporter principal and enable Object Lock for retention (if they want immutability).

Risk notes: must ensure cross-account access is narrowly scoped and that our exporter doesn't have a path to re-wrap/decrypt without customer consent. We should plan a threat model review.

If product signs up for the PoC approach above, engineering can implement the pipeline in 2-3 sprints; security will lead the threat model and key-policy template.

—Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Legal quick take:

- We can agree to a time-limited pilot exception that documents the technical controls (customer CMK usage, signed wrap records, required bucket policies, customer attestations) and an acceptance period. The exception should be narrow: pilot-only (90 days), non-precedential, and contingent on the threat model review.
- For 7-year immutability we must not commit Redwood platform to a 7-year SLA without a new product contract. Instead: we can include language that Redwood will deliver encrypted objects to the customer's S3 and provide the signed wrap records; the customer is responsible for long-term retention and immutability (Object Lock).
- Pricing/credits: recommend we include a pilot professional-services credit to cover the engineering work and a handshake commitment to revisit enterprise SLA if they convert.

I'll draft an exception addendum template; need Ben + Marissa to approve the technical bullets and Karthik's threat model to be attached.

—Lauren

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@openhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Audit log streaming + BYOK exception for HealthData retention

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Internal triage completed — high level proposal below and next steps: 

What we can pilot (timeline: PoC in 2–3 sprints, pilot agreement 90 days):
- Redwood will implement client-side envelope encryption for audit export where per-batch DEKs are wrapped using your customer CMK (you will need to grant Redwood Encrypt permissions for that CMK).
- Encrypted objects will be uploaded to your S3; Redwood will not retain plaintext copies.
- Redwood will produce signed wrap records (timestamped, keyed-hash + Redwood signature) for every batch to provide cryptographic evidence of wrap operations.
- For immutability / 7-year retention you can enable S3 Object Lock / Glacier on your bucket to meet regulatory retention; Redwood will deliver objects and records but will not assume long-term retention responsibility in the pilot.

Contract/terms: Lauren will provide a narrow pilot exception addendum (non-precedential, 90-day pilot, PS credit).

Action items: 
- Daniel: confirm you can add Redwood principal to CMK policy for Encrypt; share preferred CMK arn and S3 bucket name.
- OpenHealth Legal: confirm acceptance of proof model (we'll send sample signed wrap record).
- Marissa/Karthik: scope PoC estimate and timeline; please send ETA by end of day tomorrow.
- Ben: I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment call with OpenHealth and our security/product leads — proposed times attached.

Attaching our quick one-pager and the PoC checklist. Will follow with Lauren's draft exception for signature.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
